text:
Maya: FYI — noticed a latency spike on the canary after enabling kernel auto-switch + paged-KV heuristics. p50 for generate jumped ~20ms, p95 up ~80ms.
Alex: ugh, when did that rollout go live?
Maya: rolled at 10:03 UTC, flag `runtime.kernel_auto=on` + `kv.paged_threshold=0.6`. Canary traffic only.
Jia: can you paste the timeline & an example request shape? small-seq chat or long context?
Maya: mostly short-seq 16-64 tokens, lots of prefix cache misses (cold clients). Example request shape: user prompt 28 tokens -> completion 32 tokens.
Sam: small sequences should prefer the small-seq kernel; maybe auto-switching pushed them to FlashAttention path which has higher startup for small KV page faults.
Leo: also saw an uptick in page-faults in the profiling traces — paged-KV async prefetch not keeping up.
Maya: attaching a tiny snippet of the perf sample we captured:
```
--- perf summary ---
kernel: flash_attn_v2 (startup 2.8ms) - 45% of time
kernel: small_seq_fast (startup 0.4ms) - 22% of time
kv: page_faults/sec +120% after 10:03
latency: p95+ tail increased during spikes
```
Jia: that startup delta for flash_attn_v2 is the killer on short seqs. Even if asymptotic is better, the batching heuristics need to avoid routing small batches there.
Alex: what does the batch formation look like on the canary? token-budget targets?
Maya: current config: target_token_budget=2048, max_batch_delay=6ms, min_batch_size=3. With lots of cold requests we frequently form many tiny batches (1-2 requests) and the router picks flash_attn_v2 because of expected throughput.
Sam: suggestion: add a kernel_penalty for flash_attn when avg_seq_len < 64 OR when kv_page_fault_rate > 0.05. That would bias toward small_seq_fast.
Leo: Another lever: increase `prefetch_window_ms` for paged-KV to 12ms during canary hours; gives prefetch a bigger runway to warm pages.
Maya: ran a quick simu locally — increasing window to 12ms drops page_fault spikes but increases mem pressure slightly. tradeoff seems acceptable for canary.
perf-bot: profile diffs available: https://perf.internal/reports/2060012345/compare — shows kernel switch cost +18ms median for sequences <64.
Alex: can we A/B this? group A: kernel_penalty + small_seq bias; group B: prefetch window bump; group C: both. Keep canary traffic slice.
Sam: +1. Also add sampling traces (kv residency, kernel_choice, batch_size, avg_seq_len) for 1% of requests to get more visibility.
Jia: we should also tweak batcher to prefer coalescing tiny requests up to 8ms delay if projected token budget < 512 — that buys us better kernel utilization without blowing latency in the common case.
Maya: note: can't increase max delay indiscriminately; we have SLOs. But a conditional hold on tiny token_budget batches makes sense.
Leo: I can push a canary with three variants. will include an opt-out switch per kernel so we can revert just kernel_penalty quickly.
deploy-bot: deploy started for canary variants A/B/C at 10:47 UTC (tags: canary/kernel-kv-probes).
Maya: after 30m of traffic, A looks best: kernel_penalty alone recovers p50 & p95 almost to baseline and reduces page_faults by ~40%. B reduces page_faults but p50 is still +8ms. C similar to A.
Alex: sounds like kernel_penalty is the minimal-change win. Let's make it the default for small-seq workloads and keep prefetch_window bump as a fast rollback option.
Sam: follow-ups: 1) add telemetry metric `kernel_penalty_applied` 2) run a 4h canary at 50% production 3) add a unit/regression test in batcher sim for cold-kv small-seq traffic.
Jia: I'll open a PR for the penalty + sim test. Maya, can you assign the canary to Sam for monitoring?
Maya: assigned to Sam. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
Leo: logging note — include stack-id and kv-page-residency tag in batch traces so we can correlate page faults to model variants.
perf-bot: regression alert cleared for canary after kernel_penalty rollout.
Maya: closing loop — we'll keep small-seq bias for 72h then evaluate broader rollout.
